blocks.content: Two things need to work before the state machine feels complete.
Pausing is just a guard. When the state is not PLAYING, update() returns early and physics stop. The draw loop keeps running so the paused overlay renders smoothly on screen.
Before the ball launches, it should sit on the paddle and follow it as the player moves. That way the player can aim before committing.
You do this by overriding the ball position each frame until launch:
Once the player clicks or presses space, the ball launches with a random angle:
The angle is random within a 60 degree range so the game plays differently each round. The -Math.cos keeps the ball always moving upward on launch.
Next, you will implement the state transitions and connect everything together.
